❓ Frequently asked questions

How is the phase calculated?

From the moon's age in the 29.530588853-day synodic cycle, measured from the known new moon of 6 January 2000, 18:14 UTC. Illumination follows from (1 − cos(2π·age/cycle)) / 2.

How accurate is it?

Approximate: typically within about a day of the true phase. It is a simplified astronomical algorithm, not a full ephemeris.

What are the 8 phases?

New Moon, Waxing Crescent, First Quarter, Waxing Gibbous, Full Moon, Waning Gibbous, Last Quarter and Waning Crescent.
